title: Doubling corollary: self-covering vs free-center covering constant

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Theorem (covering bound) defines $N(A,r)$ as the minimum number of radius-$r$ balls with CENTERS IN $A$ covering $A$. The doubling corollary bounds it by $2^{\dim_d}(2\Delta/\gamma)^{\dim_d}$ via the doubling property, but the standard doubling iteration produces a cover with ARBITRARY centers. Converting to centers-in-$P_\gamma$ costs an extra factor (≈ $2^{\dim_d}$, or one more doubling step).

**Severity.** Minor — the order ($n$-independent, $(\Delta/\gamma)^{\dim_d}$) is correct; the CONSTANT should be re-derived, e.g. via a maximal $\gamma/2$-separated subset of $P_\gamma$ (automatically a same-set $\gamma/2$-net).
